_readme: Ground truth for tests/eval/corpus. Paths are relative to that directory.
type:
single         - answerable from one document
multi_domain   - needs evidence from >=2 domains (exercises source-balanced fusion)
graph_phrasing - matches _GRAPH_RE ('connection between', 'relates to', 'how is X
used') but targets documents, not code. Before the graph-fallthrough
fix these returned 3 flat-scored chunks.
There is deliberately NO 'routing' type isolating the summary signal. An earlier
draft had one, built from a document naming its topic only in its headings - but
markdown headings are body text too, so FTS indexed them and the document was
found with the summary leg switched off. The construction was measuring nothing.
More generally it cannot be constructed: a summary is derived from the body, so
the summary leg can never reach a document that chunk-level search cannot. What it
actually does is rank at the DOCUMENT level - promoting a file that is on-topic
throughout over one where a single chunk coincidentally matched. That shows up as
overall recall/nDCG, which is where the ablation asserts. Measured effect on this
corpus at k=5: solver_state_connection goes 0.67 -> 1.00 recall.
relevant_files is deliberately small and strict: a file is listed only if it
genuinely answers the query. Adding weakly-related files inflates recall and
makes the metric useless for comparing configurations.

queries.query: what does the attribute transfer node do
how do I control scatter density with an attribute
batching frames into farm tasks to amortise startup cost
why does taking the curl guarantee zero divergence
why was stale geometry served and how is the cache keyed
scene linear versus display encoded textures at ingest
turbulence octaves and how much high frequency detail to use

queries.note: docs/velocity_advection.md names the topic only in its headings and describes it in the body with different words ('carried along by whatever is moving around it'). Retained because it is a genuine vocabulary-mismatch case, but it is NOT summary-only: the headings are indexed as body text, so it is found either way.
